utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Looks like the big needs are extension cords and work gloves; duct tape’s covered, and an extra tarp would still help if one turns up.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Good to know—I’ll mention extension cords, work gloves, and maybe a spare tarp while I’m out, since folks are already covered on duct tape.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Yep, that’s it—extension cords and work gloves first, and a spare tarp if someone’s got one.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Hey Jules, I’m telling everyone the repair drive’s coming up, so bring any broken stuff by and pitch in if you can.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: That’s perfect, Vik — the community garden should make it easy for folks from both sides of the block to join in. I’ll nudge Tessa and Omar too so we can pull in a few more hands.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Great, Jules — I’m telling everyone the repair drive’s coming up, so if you see folks, remind them to bring their broken stuff by and help out.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh right, I think Saturday was the plan, but I might be mixing it up too. Maybe we should check with Mina before I turn up with the wrong tools.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Yeah, Saturday sounds right to me, but checking with Mina is probably best. I just don’t want anyone making an extra trip for nothing.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Exactly, I’d rather double-check than have us all show up at the wrong time—want me to message Mina now?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I haven’t heard a date yet, just that folks are ready to help once it’s set. If you hear anything solid, let me know.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: Will do, Rey—soon as I hear the date, I’ll pass it along. I’ve already got my tool kit ready for it.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: Thanks, Gus. Sounds like people are set to pitch in once the date comes through.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Thanks, Opal — I’m putting together a simple flow for the repair drive, and I’d really appreciate your help with check-in and keeping the volunteers organized.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Of course—I can handle check-in, and I’ll keep the volunteer list sorted by who’s coming from the corner house, across the alley, and Cedar so we know where coverage is coming from.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s perfect, Opal—thank you. Once I finish the flow, let’s do a quick walk-through together so everyone knows where to be and we can keep the day running smoothly.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Before we go any further, can we lock down where the materials are being stored and who’s responsible for missed drop-offs if people aren’t home?

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Let’s keep this one simple first, Pia—I’m just pulling together the repair list for the drive right now. Once I’ve got that, I’ll bring it by and we can sort the storage and missed drop-offs in a clear order.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I get that, but I’m not comfortable committing until those two pieces are named, because that’s exactly where these things start to unravel.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Can we confirm the storage spot first, and who’s actually coordinating drop-offs if people aren’t home?

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Yes—before we lock that in, is Faye still coordinating drop-offs, and do we know which storage spot is actually secure if people are out?

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: That’s exactly what I’m asking too—can we get a firm yes on whether Faye’s handling missed drop-offs, and which storage spot is definitely secure before we commit?

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Dane, let’s do it the same way: make a simple list of the repairs first, then we’ll line them up one by one for the drive.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sounds good—sorry I’m late again. I’ll start the list now so we can keep the line moving.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That’s fine, Dane; just keep it neat and simple. Once you’ve got the list, bring it by and we’ll set the order for the drive.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: I only caught bits and pieces—have they settled on who’s collecting tools and where folks should drop them off?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: I’m tracking the supplies side, Nell—duct tape’s covered and I’ve got one spare tarp, but extension cords and work gloves are still the big asks. I haven’t heard who’s handling tool drop-off yet.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Got it—so cords and gloves are the main gaps, and the tool drop-off’s still up in the air. If I hear anything second-hand about who’s coordinating that, I’ll pass it along.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: I think it’s still this weekend—probably Saturday—but I’d feel better if we checked with Mina so I don’t mix it up again.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: Good call—I promised to help with check-in, so I want to get it right too. Let’s check with Mina and make sure we’ve got the day and timing straight.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Yeah, that’s probably smartest—I keep thinking Saturday, but Mina will know for sure, and I’d hate to show up at the wrong time.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: We’re close, but I’d still ask around a bit more so we’re covered for intake, repairs, and cleanup without stretching anyone too thin.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Alright, I’ll ask around—how many more people do you think we need, and which role’s the thinnest right now?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I’d feel better with two or three more, and intake is the thinnest right now. If we can get one more for cleanup too, the day will run a lot smoother.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: For the repair drive, I’m thinking after school works best since I can stay through pickup; we’re mostly looking at bikes, a couple of scooters, and one stroller brake, with Amir on tools and Denise on check-in so far.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: After school works for me. I can do a pickup run first, then help sort—what time should I come by?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: That’d be great—could you come by around 3:15, once pickup starts settling, so Amir’s not juggling tools and sorting alone?

injected.text: Update: the repair drive has been moved from Saturday at the front porch to Sunday at the community center.
